name: GiveWell: cost-effectiveness of salt iodization (GAIN and ICCIDD, December 2014, moral weights updated 2021), for the Iodine Global Network
beneficiaries_note: GiveWell's model of salt iodization generally, supported by GAIN or ICCIDD (now IGN) across many low- and middle-income countries, with no country split: spread by world population.

missing_data.note: Thin: a model of salt iodization generally: the cost per person, coverage and the organisation's chance of making a difference are GiveWell's judgments, with no count of the people whose salt or iodine status IGN's support changed.

summary: GiveWell's one model of a hypothetical $100,000 donation to salt iodization through GAIN or ICCIDD (now the Iodine Global Network), built for its 2014 reviews of both and updated for its 2021 moral weights; the same sheet and rows as GAIN's page, credited here to IGN. It values iodine by children's later earnings, at 10 cents per person covered a year and a 50% chance that the organisation's support makes the difference. It is a model of salt iodization generally rather than of IGN's own spending or results, and over five years old.

story.sentence: $1,000 brings iodized salt to **{1000 * leverage_givewell / cost_per_person} people** for a year. Children who eat it grow up to earn more.

rows.label: Probability that GAIN/ICCIDD has an impact
rows.explainer: GiveWell's 50% chance that the organisation's support changes iodization outcomes (75% and 25% the alternatives), one figure for both organisations it reviewed in 2014; ICCIDD is IGN's former name. GiveWell noted that ICCIDD advises and advocates rather than running programmes, so its impact is hard to assess.
